subject: Boreas Retail: surge impact RCA & closure cadence
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@boreas-retail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@boreas-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: repeated latency & errors this morning — urgent

Hi Marcus,

We saw a large spike in tail latency and a ~7% request error rate between 04:30–05:10 PT this morning across product recommendations. Traffic returned to normal after you re-routed to the smaller model variant, but our checkout throughput dropped and a handful of orders timed out. This is hitting our peak window and we are on the hook with merchants.

Can your team share an RCA and corrective plan today? Our ops and execs are asking for immediate commitments and a clear timeline for fixes. We need:
- root cause and why the fallback to the smaller variant occurred
- mitigation already in place (what rollback/reroute you performed)
- timeline & owners for permanent fixes

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Marta

Marta Ruiz
Head of Product Operations
Boreas Retail
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@boreas-retail.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@boreas-retail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: repeated latency & errors this morning — urgent

Hi Marta — thanks for the note and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev-1 for Boreas and have the following immediate actions: 

1) Triage: Karthik is gathering kernel-level traces and KV cache metrics (started 08:45).
2) Short-term mitigation: We routed a portion of traffic to model-compact (already completed at 05:12 PT) and increased a capacity shield to preserve checkout latency while we investigate.
3) Customer comms: Laura and I will sync with your ops to align status updates and any credits needed.

I will send a draft RCA within 6 hours with owners and a 10-day remediation backlog. If that is too slow for execs, let us know and we'll accelerate.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@boreas-retail.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@boreas-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: repeated latency & errors this morning — urgent

Quick technical summary (initial findings):

- Symptom window: 04:29–05:10 PT. 95th/99th latency jumped from ~320ms to ~1.8s. Error rate hovers ~7% (client timeouts + 429 throttles).
- Root cause (prelim): interaction of unusually long sequence-length requests from a campaign (avg seq length ~1.9x typical) with our continuous-batching policy triggered large batch assemblies. That drove GPU kernel warm-ups and increased memory pressure. Memory pressure caused aggressive KV cache evictions; the cache thrash caused repeated recompute and some model variant fallbacks when OOM thresholds were approached.
- Contributing factors: a recently deployed batching change (v2.11) favoring larger max-batch for throughput, combined with an insufficient early-detection signal for KV miss storms.

Actions taken so far:
- Scaled up a temporary pool for Boreas to offload traffic (05:08).
- Forced immediate batch-size caps and reverted the max-batch knob for the affected pool (05:14).
- Collected kernel traces and a KV cache excerpt (attached: kvcache_log_excerpt.txt).

Planned corrective work (owners & ETA):
- Short term (48–72h): add a transient KV-miss alert + auto-cap batch size per-client (Owner: Karthik).
- Mid term (7–10d): introduce a sequence-length aware routing policy (route long sequences to a larger-model pool with reserved KV capacity) + refine kernel warm-up heuristics (Owner: Runtime team).
- Long term (30d): add predictive KV prefetching for known hot keys and a canary to validate v2.11 batching on tail sequences (Owner: Runtime + Release Engineering).

I'll compile a short RCA doc and share a link. Attaching the extracted logs for the subset of affected requests.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: kvcache_log_excerpt.txt

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Two asks from the account and our execs:

1) Exec readout at 11:00 PT today with Boreas leadership — Marcus, can you join and bring the 72h mitigation sprint plan?
2) Customer impact assessment: Laura (CS) needs a concise list of affected merchants and estimated order impact so Boreas can brief their merchants. Marcus / Marta, can Samir share the transaction IDs?

Notes for the remediation plan: please include a rollback-safe canary for the batching knob and a default cap at the infra level to avoid cross-tenant blast radius. Also capture the SLA credit recommendation range — I can draft a proposal after the readout.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Boreas RCA draft & closure cadence (action items + owners)

Hi all — attaching the draft RCA (boreas_rca_draft.pdf) and summarizing commitments below.

Summary: the incident was caused by a combination of unusually long incoming sequences from a marketing campaign and a recently increased max-batch preference (v2.11) which together produced KV cache thrash and kernel warm-up penalties. That led to transient OOM signals, model fallbacks, and elevated latency/error rates during the peak window.

Immediate deliverables (24–72h):
- Production: enforce per-tenant max-batch cap + transient KV-miss alert (Owner: Karthik; ETA: 48h).
- Release: create a canary gate for v2.11 batch knob constrained to 3% traffic for 72h (Owner: Release Eng; ETA: 48h).
- Customer ops: provide Boreas a merchant-impact CSV and recommended SLA credit bands (Owner: Grace & Laura; ETA: 24h).
- Follow-through: weekly remediation standup with Boreas and an exec touchpoint at day 7 (Owner: Marcus; ETA: first exec sync tomorrow 11:00 PT).

Longer-term (30d): sequence-aware routing, kernel warm-up tuning, and predictive KV prefetching (Owners: Runtime + Research).

Please see the attached draft for logs and timelines. Marta / Samir, confirm if_exec_readout_at=2027-03-14T11:00:00-07:00 works for you and we'll add the invite.
